arxiv-2211-03176.title: Fragmentation and correlations in a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate undergoing breakup
arxiv-2211-03176.creator: Sunayana Dutta, Axel U. J. Lode, Ofir E. Alon
arxiv-2211-03176.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sunayana Dutta, Axel U. J. Lode, Ofir E. Alon. The theoretical investigation of rotating Bose-Einstein condensates has mainly focused on the emergence of quantum vortex states and the condensed properties of such systems. In the present work, we concentrate on other facets by examining the impact of rotation on the ground state of weakly interacting bosons confined in anharmonic potentials computed both at the mean-field level and particularly at the many-body level of theory.

arxiv-2405-10601.title: Positive Geometries, Corolla Polynomial and Gauge Theory Amplitudes
arxiv-2405-10601.creator: Amit Suthar
arxiv-2405-10601.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Amit Suthar. Arkani-Hamed, Bai, He and Yan (ABHY) discovered a convex realisation of the associahedron whose combinatorial and geometric structure generates tree-level amplitudes in bi-adjoint scalar theory. ABHY associahedron of dimension k k determines a unique meromorphic k k -form in the kinematic space of Mandelstam invariants which is k + 3 k+3 point tree-level amplitude in bi-adjoint ϕ 3 \phi^{3} theory.

arxiv-2408-05660.title: Forecasting the accuracy of velocity-field reconstruction
arxiv-2408-05660.creator: C. Blake 1,∗, R.J. Turner 1
arxiv-2408-05660.description: Abstract Joint analyses of the large-scale distribution of galaxies, and their motions under the gravitational influence of this density field, allow powerful tests of the cosmological model, including measurement of the growth rate of cosmic structure. In this paper we perform a statistical comparison between two important classes of method for performing these tests.

arxiv-2507-22683.title: Density-functional theory study of the interaction between NV - centers and native defects in diamond
arxiv-2507-22683.creator: Gabriel I. López-Morales, Joanna M. Zajac, Tom Delord, Carlos A. Meriles, Cyrus E. Dreyer
arxiv-2507-22683.description: Abstract The NV - color center in diamond has been demonstrated as a nanoscale sensor for quantum metrology. However, the properties that make it ideal for measuring, e.g., minute electric and magnetic fields also make it sensitive to imperfections in the diamond host.

Increasing evidence has demonstrated that nicotine impairs the cardiovascular system by targeting vascular endothelial cells, but the underlying mechanisms remain obscure. It is known

pmc-10506248.title: Automatic segmentation of large-scale CT image datasets for detailed body composition analysis
pmc-10506248.creator: Nouman Ahmad, Robin Strand, Björn Sparresäter, Sambit Tarai, Elin Lundström, Göran Bergström, Håkan Ahlström, Joel Kullberg
pmc-10506248.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundBody composition (BC) is an important factor in determining the risk of type 2-diabetes and cardiovascular disease. Computed tomography (CT) is a useful imaging technique for studying BC, however manual segmentation of CT images is time-consuming and subjective.

pmc-10647783.title: Model Approach to Thermal Conductivity in Hybrid Graphene–Polymer Nanocomposites
pmc-10647783.creator: Andriy B Nadtochiy, Alla M Gorb, Borys M Gorelov, Oleksiy I Polovina, Oleg Korotchenkov, Viktor Schlosser, Victor M García-Suárez
pmc-10647783.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The thermal conductivity of epoxy nanocomposites filled with self-assembled hybrid nanoparticles composed of multilayered graphene nanoplatelets and anatase nanoparticles was described using an analytical model based on the effective medium approximation with a reasonable amount of input data. The proposed effective thickness approach allowed for the simplification of the thermal conductivity simulations in hybrid graphene@anatase TiO2 nanosheets by including the phenomenological thermal boundary resistance.

pmc-10736582.title: DEVELOPMENT OF MITOPHAGY-INDUCING SMALL MOLECULES AS THERAPEUTICS FOR AGING AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE
pmc-10736582.creator: Julie Andersen
pmc-10736582.description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia in those over the age of 65. The underlying molecular basis for the disease remains elusive. Rather than simply viewing individual diseases in isolated silos, researchers have recently turned to study of the contribution of common age-related processes to age-related diseases.

pmc-12422276.title: Easy-to-use nomogram to predict neonatal hyperbilirubinemia
pmc-12422276.creator: Shanshan Wang, Chan Wang, Siqi Zheng, Haiping Dou, Danyang Qu, Yuqian Wang, Liu Yang
pmc-12422276.description: BackgroundNeonatal hyperbilirubinemia is a common condition and a leading cause of hospitalization in newborns in their first week of life. Thus early identification of infants at risk is particularly important. In this study, we explored risk factors for its development of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia, and then constructed and validated an easy-to-use nomogram for the early prediction.

pmc-12693292.title: Enhanced Corrosion Resistance of OL 37 Steel in Hydrochloric Acid Using a Novel Composite Polymer Film
pmc-12693292.creator: Florina Branzoi, Elena Ionela Neacsu, Marius Alexandru Mihai, Alexandru Paraschiv
pmc-12693292.description: This study investigated the electrochemical deposition of a novel composite polymer, 3-methylpyrrole–sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate/3-methylthiophene (P3MPY–AOT/P3MTP), as protective coatings on OL 37 steel for anticorrosion applications. The anionic surfactant sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate used in the deposition process enhances the protective efficiency of the coating.

pmc-13238856.title: Mettl8 Regulates Hippocampal Neural Stem Cell Proliferation and Neurogenesis via mTOR/4E‐BP1 Signaling
pmc-13238856.creator: Jiamin Xu, Liping Xu, Yang Li, Xuejian Kong, Wenhui Ma, Linjie Xie, Ying Lyu, Aiguo Xuan
pmc-13238856.description: AimsHippocampal neural stem cells (NSCs) proliferation and differentiation are crucial for neuroregeneration, but their regulation remains unclear. This study investigates the role of the RNA methyltransferase Mettl8 in NSCs' fate determination.Materials and MethodsStable Mettl8‐knockdown and overexpressing NSCs lines were generated via lentiviral transduction. Gene/protein expression was analyzed by qRT‐PCR, WB, and immunofluorescence.

pmc-13361615.title: AI-Based Diagnostic Platform Capabilities With Lyme Disease as a Use Case: Integrative Exploration
pmc-13361615.creator: Sarah P Maxwell, Connie L McNeely, Abdollah Zeraatpisheh, Chris Brooks, Claire Maxwell, Kevin C Thomas, Edward Mensah
pmc-13361615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLyme disease (LD) is the most common vector-borne disease in the United States. It is difficult to diagnose because it can mimic numerous other conditions, and testing protocols may not be sufficient. Although the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommend a 2-tiered serologic testing approach for LD diagnosis, many patients are diagnosed clinically based on criteria such as the erythema migrans rash and, particularly when the rash is not present, various symptom patterns, exposure history, other information, and clinician observations.

pmc-13619202.title: Patterns of recorded sexual violence in Lithuania before and during the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13619202.creator: Diana Vasiljevaite, Jurgita Stasiuniene, Sigitas Chmieliauskas, Sigitas Laima
pmc-13619202.description: Sexual violence is a major public health and medico-legal concern, but many cases remain unreported. During the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, social isolation, restricted services, and psychosocial stress raised concerns about changes in reporting. This study aimed to analyze and compare patterns of officially recorded sexual violence in Lithuania before and during the pandemic.
